# Description

Currently `nvte_cublas_gemm_v2` requires C and D tensors to be the same, even though cublas has support for them to be different. This would allow us to fuse add to GEMM, required to fix #3741. Without this, the unfused add in PyTorch is a not performant.

## Type of change

- [ ] Documentation change (change only to the documentation, either a fix or a new content)
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Infra/Build change
- [ ] Code refactoring

## Changes

- Remove `C == D` requirement for `nvte_cublas_gemm_v2`.

nodes.diffHunk:
@@ -196,13 +196,19 @@ void nvte_cublas_gemm(const NVTETensor A, const NVTETensor B, NVTETensor D, cons
  * Computes:
  *  - `D = alpha * op(A) * op(B) + beta * C`
  *
+ * C may be the same tensor as D, in which case the result is
+ * accumulated in-place. Otherwise, C must have the same shape and
+ * dtype as D, except that FP8 output requires FP16 or BF16 C (with
+ * the same dtype as the bias, if any). FP8 output cannot be read as
+ * an accumulation input, so C is ignored if it is an FP8 D.

nodes.body: If C is in an unsupported format, we should error out rather than silently ignoring it.
NVFP4 `C` and `D` would pass this check. Instead of erroring out if `C` is FP8, it would be more robust to error out if `C` is _not_ high-precision.

None of these checks for `C` are necessary if `beta` is zero. In that case we can blindly set `C` to match `D`, similar to the old logic for FP8 output.

Unfortunately, this opens up some problems.
1. We can only check `beta` if it is on CPU.
2. We do have a config option `kNVTEMatmulConfigAlphaBetaOnDevice`. However, `alpha` must be on device for NVFP4 tensor scaling. We might want separate options to control whether `alpha` is on GPU and `beta` is on GPU.

Fixing this is more a matter of convenience than correctness. If someone is calling a GEMM with `beta=0`, it might be nice for them to pass the same tensor into `C` and `D` even if accumulation isn't supported. However, for now, the only case where `C` and `D` don't match is when `D` is FP8, in which case we can hackily workaround by passing in a dummy BF16 tensor for `C`.
